dish: A Wisconsin tap beer under the 1928 Hausler murals and 300 steins (then out to the Terrace)
address: Memorial Union, 800 Langdon St, Madison, WI 53706
w: The Memorial Union's 1928 German-style beer hall: when its first keg was tapped in 1933, UW became the first public university in the US to serve beer. Eugene Hausler's murals and riddles, restored after the union's renovation, and the 'Battle of Beer and Wine' next door in der Stiftskeller.

dish: Norwegian cookies — rosettes and krumkake — plus a monthly specialty donut
w: Stoughton's hometown bakery on Main Street in one of America's most Norwegian towns; Madison Magazine's guide to tracing Norway in Stoughton sends you here, and UpNorthNews readers voted it among Wisconsin's 13 best bakeries.

dish: French silk pie — 2,000–3,000 sold a year — from a case of a dozen-plus daily pies
w: Downtown Middleton's retro diner, whose French silk won Madison Magazine's 'Munch Madness' pie bracket; a few doors from the Mustard Museum.

dish: Cheese fondue, rösti, schnitzel and Swiss sausages
w: The Swiss table in 'America's Little Switzerland', the village founded by 108 Glarus emigrants in 1845 — fondue and rösti a short drive from New Glarus Brewing.

A family café on Mineral Point's historic High Street making the pasties that Cornish lead miners carried down the shafts in the 1830s–40s — a stop on State Trunk Tour's Wisconsin pasty-shop guide. Pair with Pendarvis.
